definition: Training a smaller “student” model to imitate the predictions of a larger “teacher” model.
details: The student learns from the teacher’s soft probability outputs rather than only hard labels, which carries richer information about similarities between classes. Distillation is a standard way to compress huge models into deployable ones while preserving much of their accuracy.

explainer.lead: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model to imitate the predictions of a larger teacher model. It matters as a standard way to compress huge models into deployable ones while preserving much of their accuracy.

tiers.eli5: A small model learns by copying the answers of a big model, including how sure it is about each option.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train the student on the teacher's soft probability outputs rather than only hard labels, because those carry richer information about class similarities. The aim is a deployable model that keeps much of the teacher's accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: The student learns from the teacher's soft probability outputs rather than only hard labels. Distillation compresses large models while preserving much of their accuracy.

explainer.example: A small student model is trained on the teacher's soft class probabilities instead of hard labels alone.

citation.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
